page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with PassMark memory scores and read-only small block memory bandwidth falling into the bottom 10%. Text processing and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and the low RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is not suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale multi-threaded applications, or LLM inference. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded processing, basic text manipulation, and simple utility services.
